newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: The 10-year bond future settled just off a new historic high, propelled by a strong performance by Bunds and T-Bonds. Inflation-friendly U.S. data also supported the market.
Short-term, traders were eyeing 133 as the next target for the notionnel after it finished the trading day up 52 ticks at 132.44, just below its intraday high of 132.50.
The bond future, which has finished higher for six straight trading sessions, ended the week up 116 basis points from last Friday.
"The only problem are the volumes which are ridiculously weak," said one trader. "On a great day like today, the Notionnel volume was 124,000 and half of that was from locals."
But he said as the market keeps climbing, investors were growing increasingly cautious.

"With the recovery seeming to happen in Europe, even if it's still fragile, the fundamentals are not as good as last year for the bond market but they are still pretty good," said an analyst. "The problem is that the curve flattening we're seeing right now can't last forever."
"So we're bound to see a correction. The question is when and how," he said.
For one trader, Friday's settlement near the day's highs bode well for next week as he had no worries about the most crucial U.S. number expected next week -- January inflation due on Wednesday.

He said that if the T-bond managed to keep its positive orientation by the end of trade on Friday, "we can look toward the notionnel at 133. After that, it will perhaps be time for a bit of a correction," he said.
On the cash market, the yield on the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT fell to 5.31 percent from 5.38 percent. On the new OAT 5.50 percent 2007, the yield was at 5.395 percent.
U.S. markets are closed on Monday for President's Day.
